content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Explain how sperm reach and penetrate the egg
Describe the formation of the zygote
is the fusion of male and female gamete nuclei to form a zygote. It usually occurs in the oviduct. After fertilisation, the zygote divides and travels to the uterus, where
occurs. These events are critical for a pregnancy to begin.
Changes sperm undergo in female tract that enable fertilisation
Sperm binds to zona pellucida (egg coat)
Sperm membrane fuses with egg membrane
Sperm and egg nuclei approach each other
Only one sperm should fertilise egg
Fast block and slow block to polyspermy
Half genetic material from each parent
Sperm survive ~3-5 days in female tract
Fertilisation must occur within this window
Hollow ball with inner cell mass
Cilia in oviduct waft it along
Embedding of blastocyst into endometrium (uterine lining)
It occurs in the oviduct (Fallopian tube)
The fastest sperm fertilises the egg
It takes many sperm to break down barriers; one then enters
Twins form from the same fertilisation event
Identical twins do; fraternal twins come from two eggs
Fusion of sperm and egg nuclei
Hollow ball of cells that implants
Embedding of blastocyst in uterus lining
Sperm travel from vagina through uterus to oviduct
Only ~100-200 of millions of sperm reach the egg
Acrosome enzymes help sperm penetrate egg
Zygote divides to form morula then blastocyst
Blastocyst travels to uterus over ~5 days
hCG production signals pregnancy has begun
